content: #2 The people at math.SE have commenting on your claim, I think the experts on this topic are more likely to be there than here, so we very likely have nothing to add informed by scrutiny of the mathematical claims. Additionally, I infer from ‘SBK’s comment that they may well be one such expert. That your proof initially seemed to rely on AI-generated text from Grok, and that you recognised at one point that one iteration of this was wrong, doesn’t fill me with confidence in the very bold claim that would indicate several generations of mathematicians missed an error in the proof of the theorem, including some of the best in the world.

content:
#3 Victor, I sense that ultimately you are really interested in chatting about math, which is a good cause.

What makes you come across as a madman, though, is that you cast any random thought that crosses your mind as a bold claim.

Like, in the original thread here, you started by bluntly claiming that the conjecture is trivially false. After I pointed out to you that your argument missed the most basic facts about the Hausdorff measure, within hours you turned around and claimed a “complete proof” of the conjecture. Then a couple of days later you claimed a counterexample.

If this chain of thoughts of yours had been cast as questions, they could actually be appropriate for a discussion forum like here, where it’s allowed, and even welcome, for people to exchange half-baked thoughts on matters worth learning — and it’s common human nature that one progresses through a chain of silly ideas to, eventually, an actual understanding of a matter.

So before we block you for good, consider changing your style of communication. Ask questions and don’t force your last night’s thought into the references section of an nLab entry.
subject: Kakeya disproved?
